_readme: Each module is a scoring model, not a category label. A generic scraper returns everyone in the county; a module ranks them by whether they need the work right now. Signal weights within a module must sum to exactly 1.0 — check.mjs enforces it — so a score is always 0-100 and always comparable across modules.
_normalisation: type=numeric normalises linearly across `range` then inverts when direction is 'lower'. type=boolean is 1 or 0. type=band is piecewise, for relationships that are not monotonic — a 5-year-old roof and a 45-year-old roof are both bad roofing leads, for opposite reasons, and a linear model cannot express that.

modules.name: Roofing
modules.summary: Ranks by roof age against storm history, weighted by whether a claim is realistically payable.
modules.thesis: A roofing lead is not a house. It is a roof old enough to fail, that took hail recently enough to claim, owned by somebody who can authorise the work.

signals.label: Roof age

bands.note: Under warranty. Not a lead.
Asphalt's replacement window.
Likely already replaced without a permit, or a neglected rental.

signals.derivation: Most recent roofing permit; falls back to year built when no permit exists.

signals.label: Hail events, 3 years
signals.derivation: NOAA storm reports of 1in+ hail within 3km of the parcel centroid.

bands.note: Deferred maintenance risk — wants it, often cannot fund it.
Tends to go to specialty and architectural roofers.

signals.label: Owner-occupied
signals.derivation: Mailing address matches situs address. The single strongest predictor of who can say yes on a doorstep.

signals.label: Claim likelihood
signals.derivation: hail severity x roof age x material vulnerability. Marketing suitability only — never an insurance eligibility determination.

modules.outreachAngle: Reference the storm date, not the roof. 'The 14 May hail ran right through your street' outperforms 'your roof looks old' by a wide margin, because one is a fact they remember and the other is an insult.

modules.name: Solar
modules.summary: Ranks by generation potential against payback period, not by who owns a house.
modules.thesis: Solar sells on payback maths. A perfect south-facing roof in a cheap-power state is a worse lead than a mediocre roof where power costs 28c.

signals.label: Shading
signals.derivation: Canopy and structure occlusion over the usable roof plane, annualised.

signals.label: Local electricity rate
signals.derivation: The signal most installers ignore and the one that actually closes deals.

signals.label: Income bracket
signals.derivation: Census block-group median, never an individual estimate. Modelled area data, so it cannot be used for any eligibility decision.

bands.note: Panels outlive the roof — a new roof is the ideal substrate.
Needs a re-roof first. Sell the roofer a referral instead.

modules.outreachAngle: Lead with the bill, not the panels. An estimated monthly saving figure beats every environmental pitch ever written.

modules.name: Lawn & Landscape
modules.summary: Ranks by lot size and visible turf condition against ability to pay for recurring service.
modules.thesis: Recurring revenue lives on big lots owned by people who are time-poor, not money-poor. Route density beats lead count — twenty jobs on one street is worth more than sixty scattered across a county.

bands.note: Mows it themselves in twenty minutes.
Quarter acre to an acre — the recurring-contract sweet spot.
Acreage. Different equipment, different quote.

signals.label: Turf condition
signals.derivation: Vegetation index over the parcel's lawn polygon versus the block median. Below-block-median greenness during growing season means neglect, and neglect means an unserviced lot.

signals.label: HOA likelihood
signals.derivation: Subdivision plat age and uniformity plus a registered HOA entity at the same plat. HOAs enforce standards, and enforcement is what converts a maybe into a contract.

signals.label: Season timing
signals.derivation: Local growing-degree-day accumulation against the contract-signing window. Ranks the same list differently in March than in September, which is the entire point.

modules.outreachAngle: Sell the route, not the yard. 'We already cut four houses on your street on Thursdays' closes because it is cheap for you and convenient for them.

modules.name: HVAC
modules.summary: Ranks by estimated system age against the weather about to hit it.
modules.thesis: HVAC is bought in a panic. The whole game is finding the fifteen-year-old system the week before a heat dome, not selling maintenance in October.

signals.label: System age

bands.note: Failure window for residential split systems.
Running on borrowed time or already swapped off-permit.

signals.derivation: Most recent mechanical permit; falls back to year built.

signals.label: Emergency likelihood
signals.derivation: System age x 7-day extreme-temperature forecast. This is the signal that justifies a same-day call rather than a postcard.

modules.outreachAngle: Time it to the forecast. A replacement offer that lands 72 hours before a heat wave converts several times better than the identical offer in mild weather.

modules.name: Commercial Property
modules.summary: Ranks by roof type and maintenance cycle, and tells you whether the occupant can even sign.
modules.thesis: Commercial fails on the wrong contact, not the wrong building. Tenant versus owner is worth more than every physical signal combined.

signals.label: Decision authority
signals.derivation: Assessor owner name matched against the registered entity trading at the address. A triple-net tenant pays for the roof; a gross-lease tenant cannot authorise a nail.

signals.label: Maintenance cycle due
signals.derivation: Time since last permit against the typical service interval for that building type and roof system.

modules.outreachAngle: Get to the entity, not the storefront. Match the assessor's owner name to the Secretary of State filing and you have a registered agent who answers letters.

modules.name: Auto Repair
modules.summary: Ranks blocks, not driveways — where the out-of-warranty cars are.
modules.thesis: You cannot see somebody's car from a data feed and you should not try. This module works at block-group level and targets neighbourhoods whose fleet has aged out of warranty.

bands.note: Dealer warranty. Not yours yet.
Out of warranty, still worth repairing.
Repair cost starts exceeding value.

signals.label: Repeat service likelihood
signals.derivation: Residential tenure and fleet age. Long-tenure households produce repeat customers; transient ones do not.

signals.label: Income bracket

bands.note: Defers repairs.
Repairs rather than replaces. The core independent-shop customer.
Leases new, services at the dealer.

signals.derivation: Census block-group median, never an individual estimate. Marketing suitability only — an area figure used to decide who gets credit or a policy makes the output a consumer report.

signals.label: Commute distance
signals.derivation: Miles cause wear. Long-commute block groups generate service intervals twice as often.

modules.outreachAngle: Geographic, not personal. Direct mail and geofenced ads to a scored block group — anything that implies you know what car sits in their driveway reads as surveillance and backfires.

modules.name: General Contractor
modules.summary: Ranks by permit activity and owner equity — who is already spending, and who can borrow against the house.
modules.thesis: Renovation is funded from equity. A permit pulled six months ago says a homeowner is mid-project and has a budget open right now.

signals.label: Recent permits
signals.derivation: An open or recent permit is the single highest-intent public signal available anywhere. Nothing else comes close.

signals.label: Owner equity
signals.derivation: Assessed value against recorded deed and lien amounts, decayed on a standard amortisation curve. Public-record modelling for marketing suitability — it is not a credit report and must never be used to decide who gets financing.

bands.note: First major refresh — kitchens and baths.
Systems, envelope and layout all due.
Historic. Higher value, more permitting friction.

signals.label: Renovation likelihood
signals.derivation: Recent sale plus property age plus neighbourhood permit rate. Houses renovate within eighteen months of changing hands far more often than at any other time.

bands.note: Just moved in. Everything is getting changed.
Settled, equity built, systems failing.

modules.outreachAngle: Permit records are public and timestamped. Reaching a homeowner the week their permit is issued puts you ahead of every contractor still knocking doors cold.

modules.name: Insurance
modules.summary: Ranks by life events that force a policy decision — a move, a purchase, a new business.
modules.thesis: Nobody shops insurance because they were asked. They shop it because something changed. Find the change.
modules.regulatoryNote: Every signal here is marketing-suitability only. None may be used to decide eligibility, rate, or terms — that use makes the output a consumer report under the FCRA and this platform is not a consumer reporting agency. The scoring engine refuses to expose signals flagged `restricted` until the account records an attestation; see compliance.ts.

signals.label: Life event
signals.derivation: Public filings only. A new LLC needs general liability within about thirty days of formation, and almost nobody calls them.

signals.label: Recent home purchase
signals.derivation: Deed recorded in the last 90 days. Homeowner's policy is mandatory at closing and shopped hard in the window right after.

signals.label: Carrier churn risk
signals.derivation: Carrier rate-filing increases in the state and ZIP against typical renewal timing. When a carrier files a 14% increase, that book shops in the following quarter.

signals.label: Vehicles in household
signals.derivation: Block-group aggregate. Multi-vehicle households are where bundling actually pays.

modules.outreachAngle: Speed decides it. A new-LLC filing is worth calling the same week; at ninety days somebody else has already written the policy.
